title: Telephone Number Allocation Credential
description: Telephone Number Allocation credential proves an enterprise has the right to use (RTU) specific telephone numbers, either directly from a regulator or through a telephone number provider.

v.description: Version string using ACDC conventions, encoding protocol, serialization, and size.

d.description: SAID of the credential (Blake3-256 digest in CESR compact encoding).

u.description: A salty nonce (high-entropy random value) used to prevent rainbow-table attacks on the credential SAID.

i.description: AID of the issuer (the party asserting the telephone number allocation right).

ri.description: SAID of the issuer's ACDC credential status registry.

s.description: SAID of this schema (Blake3-256 digest in CESR compact encoding).

d.description: SAID of the attributes block (Blake3-256 digest in CESR compact encoding).

u.description: A salty nonce for the attributes block, enabling selective disclosure.

i.description: AID of the credential recipient — the enterprise or individual that holds the right to use the allocated telephone numbers.

dt.description: Issuance date-time (when the ACDC was signed), as an ISO-8601 datetime string with timezone.

numbers.description: Array of number expressions representing telephone numbers allocated to the enterprise. Each expression is either a single E164 number (e.g., '+15551234567') or an inclusive range denoted by a hyphen between two E164 numbers (e.g., '+15551230000-+15551239999'). All numbers in a single credential must share the same granting authority.

items.description: A single E164 telephone number or an inclusive range. Single number: '+' followed by 7-15 digits. Range: two E164 numbers separated by a hyphen (e.g., '+15551230000-+15551239999').

channel.description: Optional list of communication channels for which these numbers are allocated. If omitted, no channel restriction is implied. Use 'sms' for A2P/P2P messaging, 'voice' for voice calls, or both to indicate dual-channel use.

startDate.description: Optional start date from which the telephone number allocation is valid (ISO-8601). Useful for proving long-term continuous ownership of a number.

endDate.description: Optional expiration date of the telephone number allocation (ISO-8601). If omitted, the allocation is considered open-ended and subject only to credential revocation.

tnalloc.description: Chain to a telephone number allocation (RTU) credential that proves with a valid chain back to the regulator

n.description: SAID of a parent telephone number allocation credential that grants the issuer the right to sub-allocate.

s.description: SAID of the telephone number allocation schema that the chained credential must satisfy.

o.description: Issuer-To-Issuee, operator indicating issuer AID of this ACDC MUST be the Issuee AID of the node this Edge points to.

issuer.description: Credential that proves the identity of the issuer.

n.description: SAID of a credential that proves the identity of the issuer (e.g., an Org Identity or vLEI credential).

s.description: SAID of the schema that the issuer identity credential must satisfy.

o.description: Edge operator. I2I (default): issuer AID MUST be the issuee AID of the node this edge points to. NI2I: issuer AID MAY or MAY NOT be the issuee AID of that node. DI2I: issuer AID MUST be the issuee AID or a delegated AID of the issuee AID of that node. NOT: inverts the validity of the node this edge points to.

oneOf.description: SAID of rules block (Blake3-256 digest in CESR compact encoding)

governance.description: Statement identifying the governance framework under which this credential was issued.

oneOf.default: Issuees agree not to share or lend the allocated telephone number(s) to other parties in a way that would make it difficult to consistently identify the originator of traffic.

l.default: Issuees agree not to share or lend the allocated telephone number(s) to other parties in a way that would make it difficult to consistently identify the originator of traffic.
